Barry: "Watch..."

Barry This [Cmin7] diminished... there are 4 dominants. What were the four dominants? You tell me....
[student answers] "B, D, G, and Ab"
Barry: Right. You got that?
Barry: Okay... B, D, F, and Ab. They are roots that form another diminished...

Barry: So now what is a diminished scale?
Barry: A diminished scale is the combination of the diminished chord and its 4 dominant roots.
Barry: So here's the C diminished, and here's the B diminished. And you just to this [Barry folds his fingers to show how they are combined].
Barry: So the scale is...
Barry: So there's your scale.
Barry: Now, the interesting things about this is this. You start making up things. Watch.... "C" is surrounded by what?
Barry: "C" is surrounded by what?...
[27:31] Barry: If I do it with one hand, it'll be like this:
I'll borrow.. watch... I'll borrow that tonic of the dominant... [i.e. "b" is root of a 'B' dominant chord]
I made it go home...
So if I say....
[i.e. Ab is root of Ab7]
[i.e. "f" is root of F7']
[i.e. "d" is root of D7]
You see that?
So I say:Ahh, each note is surrounded by two....
each note is surrounded by that....
[i.e. "f" and "Ab" are roots of F7 and Ab7]
So now I'll learn how to do...
[i.e. these are the notes of a diminished 7 chord AND the roots of the four dominant chords in the family of that dim 7 chord]
So I've go all of this...
I've got a whole lot of things.... so I can say...
My first run should be something like....
If I did two of them I would say......
[I.e., Barry is "borrowing" TWO notes at the same time, from 2 of the roots of the 4 dominant chords related to the diminished 7 chord]
Then you're gonna hear some cat, and he's gonna say....
All these things come from one thing....they come from this "diminished"
and "SURROUNDING"...
See, you "SURROUND" the notes....
See, the roots of the dominants say.... "take me home"..
But now, I might not borrow THAT one. I [might] borrow THE ONE BELOW that is probably more [homesick?].
So now what I got is this....
So I got a lot of things, you know. So you end up with a whole lot of things. You learn to BORROW.
See, what you got there is what you call a "drop 2". You should know how to do that.
The A is "soprano (1)" The Gb is "tenor (2)" The Eb is "alto (3)" The C is "bass (4)"
"Drop 2"
"Drop 3" [Barry by mistake says Drop 4]
"Drop 2, 4"
See all this...
It's different now.... The A is now "soprano The Eb" is now tenor The Gb is now alto The C is now bass That's how you mix them up...
That's pretty.
See [i.e. watch] how I can do those things....
If I did TWO things.. let's see...
That's [beats 1,2] the roots of the dominants. Watch [beats 3,4] I take it to the diminished.
That's the way it is.... you start doing stuff... You start doing things, you know?
